title: The 10-Year Delay That Costs $400,130

beats.say: Starting to invest at 25 instead of 35 changes your final net worth more than you think.
beats.visual: A cinematic shot of a vintage desk clock ticking in a dimly lit room, moody shadows, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: Here's the exact math behind the 10-year delay that quietly drains your future account.
beats.visual: Close-up of a hand moving a wooden chess piece across a dark board, moody ambient side lighting.

beats.say: If you invest $200 a month at 8% a year starting at age 25, you reach age 65 with a massive total.
beats.visual: A sleek modern metal lamp casting a warm circle of light onto a clean, empty wooden tabletop.

beats.say: That monthly habit compounds over 40 years into a balance of $698,202 sitting in your portfolio.
beats.visual: A close-up of dark espresso coffee being poured into a matte black ceramic mug, slow motion, moody lighting.

beats.say: Now let's look at what happens if you wait just 10 years until age 35 to start.
beats.visual: An open leather-bound notebook lying flat on a dark mahogany desk, pages blank, soft window light.

beats.say: You still put away that same $200 a month at 8% a year, but you only have 30 years left.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person standing by a large factory window, looking out at a hazy morning skyline.

beats.say: That shorter timeline drops your final balance down to $298,072 by the time you reach age 65.
beats.visual: A brass hourglass resting on a dark slate surface, fine white sand slowly falling through the center.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions when they tell you to wait until your career is fully settled.
beats.visual: A close-up of a heavy iron key lying on a distressed wooden workbench, moody overhead spotlight.

beats.say: Subtract those two final amounts and you'll find a difference of exactly $400,130 lost to time.
beats.visual: Raindrops sliding down a tall glass window pane at night, blurred city lights glowing softly in the background.

beats.say: Waiting a decade doesn't just cost you 10 years of deposits, it destroys your greatest compounding multiplier and that's exactly how
beats.visual: A dark silhouette of a person walking down a quiet hallway toward a warm sliver of light under a closed door.

caption:
Time is your only real asset in the market. Start early, even with small amounts.
